newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MPs reject second Ciller graft charge.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MPs reject second Ciller graft charge.

text.p: Turkish MPs voted against sending Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court in the second of two corruption charge votes she faced on Tuesday.
Deputy speaker Kamer Genc announced that deputies voted 271 to 257 against impeaching Ciller for her alleged illegal interference with the sale of state-owned carmaker TOFAS.

"So there is no need for the concerned (Ciller) to go to the Supreme Court," Genc said. A parliamentary commission looking into the allegations had recommended dropping the charges against Ciller, premier from 1993 to 1996.
MPs earlier on Tuesday rejected a first, less serious charge alleging Ciller failed to prevent corruption at the TEDAS electricity company. MPs voted 327 to 172 against that charge.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist-led government would have been in deep trouble if coalition partner Ciller lost either of the votes. The government has 279 MPs in the 550-seat parliament.

Ciller, also the foreign minister, faces a further corruption vote in parliament on Wednesday on the source of her substantial personal wealth. The government must also deal with an opposition censure motion next week.
